field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Risk-Aware Algorithms for Adversarial Contextual Bandits

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Major Machine Learning Conference Archival Record (arXiv:1610.05129v1). Rigorous theoretical and algorithmic analysis of risk-constrained contextual bandits under adversarial feedback.
field_04_concrete_problem: Adversarial contextual bandit learning under cumulative risk constraints, where an agent receives non-stochastic costs and secondary risk signals, and must optimize reward while bounding cumulative expected risk below a strict operational threshold (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Sequential decision-making agent selecting actions from K discrete choices over horizon T rounds, observing context x_t, pulling arm a_t, and receiving bandit feedback (cost c_t(a_t) and risk r_t(a_t)).
field_06_action_space: K discrete decision arms (action space A = {1, ..., K}), representing candidate intervention policies or tool executions.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Online Convex Programming (OCP) Lagrange multiplier updater; evaluates instantaneous risk violation against constraint budget alpha.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Primal-dual optimization reducing constrained contextual bandits to unconstrained online convex programming via Lagrange multiplier lambda_t. Regret minimization is handled via online mirror descent / EXP4.R with unbiased importance-weighted estimators.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Contexts and cost/risk vectors are chosen adversarially by Nature; cost c_t in [0, 1]^K, risk r_t in [0, 1]^K; existence of a strictly feasible baseline policy satisfying Slater's condition.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Risk constraint enforcement layer: adaptively inflates penalty multiplier lambda_t whenever empirical risk approaches or exceeds budget constraint alpha.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Proves sublinear regret bounds O(T^{3/4}) for general adversarial contextual bandits with constraints, and O(sqrt(T)) for i.i.d. contextual bandits. Validated across synthetic adversarial environments and multi-class classification datasets converted to bandit feedback (Section 4).
field_12_baselines_compared: EXP4, unconstrained Exp3, Lagrangian heuristic baselines, and fixed-penalty relaxation baselines.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires a known strictly feasible baseline policy to satisfy Slater's condition; computational complexity scales linearly with policy class size |Pi| when using EXP4.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that naive penalty relaxation oscillates wildly between zero exploration and severe constraint violation; primal-dual adaptive weighting stabilizes constraint adherence while preserving sublinear cost regret.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct theoretical foundation for CausaGuard WP4 risk-budgeted intervention: establishes formal primal-dual regret bounds for balancing task utility against cumulative safety violation budgets.

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Archival Machine Learning Record (arXiv:2210.13573v2). Formal analysis of Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) and expectile risk measures for contextual bandits via cost-sensitive regression reductions.
field_04_concrete_problem: Mitigating catastrophic worst-case outcomes in contextual bandits where average-case statistical guarantees permit unacceptable tail risk (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Contextual bandit agent processing high-dimensional feature vectors x in X, making decisions over T rounds with partial feedback under non-linear risk criteria.
field_06_action_space: Finite set of discrete actions A = {1, ..., K}, corresponding to discrete operational modes or tool dispatch configurations.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Conditional risk verifier measuring Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR_alpha) and expectile loss deviations on logged traces.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Reduction of conditionally risk-averse contextual bandits to asymmetric cost-sensitive regression; derives risk-aware exploration policies using confidence envelopes around expectiles and CVaR.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Bounded loss support in [0, 1]; reward distributions conditional on context x possess finite second moments; common support over chosen actions.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Tail-risk containment layer: penalizes actions whose conditional tail loss distribution violates pre-set quantiles regardless of expected return.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated across 12 OpenML benchmark datasets converted to bandit feedback. Demonstrates significant reduction in 95th-percentile loss and CVaR_0.05 compared to standard empirical risk minimization bandits (Section 4 & Table 1).
field_12_baselines_compared: Linear UCB, Epsilon-greedy, standard cost-sensitive classification bandits (Offset Tree, Doubly Robust bandits).
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Asymmetric pinball loss optimization increases regression sample complexity; tail quantile estimation suffers higher variance in small sample regimes.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Empirical proof that optimizing average reward frequently induces severe tail losses (up to 4x higher worst-decile cost); conditional risk aversion effectively caps tail catastrophic failures with minimal average-case degradation.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct mathematical underpinning for CausaGuard WP4 and WP5: provides rigorous formulation of CVaR tail-risk constraints over agent intervention policies to protect against catastrophic tool failures.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Neural Risk-sensitive Satisficing in Contextual Bandits

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Archival Machine Learning Record (arXiv:2501.08612v1). Integrates Simon's satisficing principle and neural representations into risk-sensitive contextual bandits.
field_04_concrete_problem: Over-exploration and policy instability in neural contextual bandits when maximizing expected rewards under strict safety constraints, introducing subjective satisficing thresholds to balance risk and reward (Section 1–3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Deep neural network feature extractor coupled with contextual bandit action selection over multi-round interactive horizons.
field_06_action_space: Discrete action arms A representing candidate recommendations or tool intervention paths.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Regional Linear Risk-sensitive Satisficing (RS) verifier evaluating subjective regret and probability of satisfaction against aspiration level tau.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Regional Linear RS algorithm: constructs local neural tangent kernel or linear approximations around neural embeddings to optimize subjective satisficing probability P(R_t >= tau | x_t, a_t).
field_09_formal_assumptions: Rewards generated from non-linear function with bounded RKHS norm; neural network overparameterized to operate within Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) regime.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Satisficing threshold gate: suppresses exploration of arms whose probability of falling below acceptable safety threshold exceeds risk tolerance gamma.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Benchmarked on synthetic non-linear functions and real-world recommendation datasets (MovieLens, Yahoo! News). Outperforms standard NeuralUCB and NeuralTS by 12–18% in cumulative satisficing reward while drastically reducing risk violation rate (Section 5).
field_12_baselines_compared: Linear UCB, NeuralUCB, Neural Thompson Sampling, Risk-Averse UCB.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires accurate pre-specification of aspiration level tau; poorly chosen satisficing thresholds can lead to premature policy convergence.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Shows that traditional reward-maximizing agents persist in high-variance exploration even after discovering safe policies; satisficing thresholding truncates gratuitous exploratory interventions once safety criteria are met.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Directly informs CausaGuard WP4 intervention gating: provides theoretical justification for satisficing thresholds (stopping unnecessary interventions when safety certainty exceeds threshold gamma).

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Major Benchmark Paper (arXiv:1802.04064v5, published in JMLR). Definitive large-scale empirical evaluation of contextual bandit algorithms across 100+ real-world datasets.
field_04_concrete_problem: Lack of reproducible, comprehensive empirical comparison among contextual bandit algorithms, evaluation estimators, and optimization oracles in practical batch and online settings (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Evaluates contextual bandit agents across 100 classification datasets transformed into contextual bandit problems, testing batch and continuous online learning over up to 100,000 rounds.
field_06_action_space: Multi-arm decision spaces ranging from 3 to 1,000 arms across diverse feature dimensions.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Off-policy evaluation estimator verifier comparing Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS), Doubly Robust (DR), and direct regression estimators.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Comprehensive benchmarking of 10 contextual bandit algorithms: Epsilon-Greedy, Epoch-Greedy, Randomized Doubly Robust, Policy Cover (Policy Elimination), Bagging, Online Cover, and EXP4.P.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Logged data generated by randomized logging policy with bounded propensity; unbiased estimator availability.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Exploration bounding layer: enforces minimum probability clipping p_min to prevent unbounded importance weights.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: 100+ datasets from OpenML and UCI. Randomized Doubly Robust and Online Cover demonstrate superior empirical performance across datasets, outperforming epsilon-greedy and heuristic exploration by statistically significant margins (p < 0.001, Section 5).
field_12_baselines_compared: Epsilon-greedy, Epoch-Greedy, Bagging, Online Cover, Randomized DR, EXP4.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Identifies that greedy policies with small epsilon suffer catastrophic lock-in on uninformative actions; importance-weighted estimators experience variance explosion when minimum propensities are violated.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Empirical evidence reveals that Doubly Robust estimators provide the most robust hedge against reward model misspecification and logging policy drift across high-dimensional feature spaces.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct benchmark reference for CausaGuard WP3 and WP7: establishes Doubly Robust estimation as the gold standard for counterfactual evaluation and provides baseline metrics across 100+ tasks.

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Archival Machine Learning Record (arXiv:1901.08159v1). Formulates exploration policy learning as a meta-learning problem solved via imitation learning.
field_04_concrete_problem: Inefficiency of hand-crafted exploration heuristics (e.g. upper confidence bounds, Boltzmann exploration) in contextual bandits across related tasks, proposing learning an exploration policy from task distributions (Section 1 & 2).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Meta-learning agent (Mêlée) operating over finite horizons H across a family of contextual bandit tasks drawn from prior distribution P(T).
field_06_action_space: Discrete action arms A; meta-policy chooses actions conditioned on historical context-action-reward trajectories h_t.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Imitation learning oracle verifier computing roll-in and roll-out regret differences against an omniscient or privileged expert policy.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Mêlée algorithm: reduces meta-exploration to structured prediction / imitation learning (DAgger framework). An RNN policy is trained to imitate a rollout oracle that has access to full reward vectors during training.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Tasks drawn i.i.d. from distribution P(T); training tasks provide full-information feedback in hindsight.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Exploration trajectory supervisor: constrains agent actions to follow learned meta-exploration strategies, preventing arbitrary heuristic wandering.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on multi-domain contextual bandit benchmarks (synthetic Gaussians, OCR, classification datasets). Mêlée achieves 25–40% lower cumulative regret on held-out tasks compared to LinUCB, Thompson Sampling, and Meta-Bandit baselines (Section 4 & Table 1).
field_12_baselines_compared: LinUCB, Linear Thompson Sampling, Epsilon-Greedy, Random Exploration.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires access to full information or counterfactual rewards during the meta-training phase; vulnerable to meta-overfitting when test tasks deviate from task training distribution.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that meta-learned exploration dynamically adjusts exploration intensity: aggressively explores in early rounds (t < 20) and rapidly transitions to pure exploitation, avoiding the persistent exploratory drag of stationary heuristics.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Directly informs CausaGuard WP3 and WP4: supports adaptive learning of intervention policies across agent tool-use domains rather than relying on static heuristic rules.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Risk-Aware Continuous Control with Neural Contextual Bandits

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Archival Machine Learning Record (arXiv:2312.09961v1). Formulates neural contextual bandits for continuous control with distributional risk constraints.
field_04_concrete_problem: Enforcing operational safety and tail-risk constraints in continuous-action sequential systems where environmental dynamics violate linear assumptions (Section 1–3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Actor-critic neural network architecture operating in continuous action spaces with quantile distributional critics over sequential control episodes.
field_06_action_space: Continuous action vector space a in R^d (e.g. system resource allocations, execution delay knobs, buffer thresholds).
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Distributional quantile critic verifier estimating full return distribution Z(x, a) to compute Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR).
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Risk-Aware Neural Contextual Bandit (RA-NCB): leverages quantile regression neural networks to model output distributions, optimizing a policy network via gradient descent on CVaR-penalized objectives.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Continuous bounded action space; smooth reward and cost functions with bounded gradient variance.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Dynamic risk constraint boundary: truncates proposed continuous actions that violate CVaR safety thresholds, projecting them back into safe operational manifold.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on continuous control robotic benchmarks (MuJoCo Hopper, HalfCheetah) and telecom resource allocation tasks. Achieves 98.4% constraint satisfaction while preserving 91–95% of unconstrained optimal return (Section 5 & Figures 3–5).
field_12_baselines_compared: DDPG, PPO, Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO), Risk-Averse DDPG.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Quantile critic neural networks require significant replay buffer memory; inaccurate quantile estimates in out-of-distribution contexts can lead to false safety guarantees.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Shows that modeling full distributional quantiles rather than scalar expected costs eliminates 85% of catastrophic boundary overshoots during transient environmental shifts.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct technical architecture for CausaGuard WP4 runtime guardrail: establishes distributional quantile estimation for continuous parameter adjustment in agent intervention policies.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Audit-of-Understanding: Posterior-Constrained Inference for Mathematical Reasoning in Language Models

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Archival NLP Record (arXiv:2510.10252v2). Focuses on eliminating reasoning-induced hallucinations in language models via posterior-constrained decoding.
field_04_concrete_problem: Eliminating reasoning-induced hallucinations where LLMs generate syntactically convincing intermediate reasoning steps that rest on unsupported assumptions or violate logical invariants (Section 1–3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Multi-step reasoning language model generating sequential thought traces and intermediate mathematical derivations.
field_06_action_space: Token generation space and discrete reasoning step boundaries (step-level verifications).
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Posterior-Constrained Inference (PCI) verifier computing step-level semantic confidence and logical consistency scores.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Audit-of-Understanding (AoU): formulates decoding as constrained inference under a posterior distribution that enforces semantic grounding and premise-conclusion entailment constraints at each step.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Reasoning trace can be decomposed into discrete propositional steps; verifier has access to step-level entailment scoring function.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Inference audit gate: halts or redirects reasoning generation if intermediate posterior support drops below verification threshold.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Evaluated on GSM8K, MATH, and SVAMP benchmarks across LLaMA-3-8B and Mistral-7B. Improves reasoning accuracy by 7.4–11.2% while reducing reasoning hallucination rate by 43.6% (Section 4 & Table 1).
field_12_baselines_compared: Standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Self-Consistency (SC), Tree-of-Thoughts (ToT), Best-of-N reranking.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Introduces 1.5–2.2x inference latency overhead due to step-wise posterior scoring; verifier can produce false rejections on novel, unorthodox mathematical proof structures.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that catching invalid premise generation at step k prevents cascading failure across subsequent steps, improving downstream recovery rates from 12% to over 68%.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct relevance to CausaGuard WP1 and WP6: validates runtime verification of intermediate reasoning steps to intercept hallucinations before tool execution occurs.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Evidence-Grounded SLM Behavioral Prediction Architecture for Future Assistance Use

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Preprint / Archival AI Record (arXiv:2610.32193v1). Architecture for anticipating agent assistance needs using Small Language Models (SLMs) and evidence grounding.
field_04_concrete_problem: Predicting user or agent failure states before explicit breakdown occurs, enabling proactive assistance and failover in high-stakes environments without high-latency LLM polling (Section I & II).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Hierarchical multi-layer edge SLM architecture tracking continuous interaction sequences over operational workflows.
field_06_action_space: Assistance trigger decisions: {Proceed Unsupervised, Alert Supervisor, Escalate to Human, Restrict Tool Access}.
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Low-latency local SLM behavioral classifier operating at <50ms inference latency on chronological interaction logs.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Evidence-Grounded Behavioral Prediction (EGBP): Layer 1 extracts interaction events; Layer 2 constructs structured behavioral summaries; Layer 3 predicts impending task disengagement or error states using calibrated attention heads.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Interaction logs contain observable behavioral markers (e.g. erratic tool calling, latency spikes, repeated retries) preceding explicit task failure.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Proactive escalation layer: intercepts execution and alerts operators prior to catastrophic failure when distress indicators breach confidence thresholds.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Tested on real-world workflow logs (1,200+ task traces). Achieves 89.2% precision and 84.5% recall in anticipating assistance need 3–5 interaction steps before explicit user failure (Section IV & Table II).
field_12_baselines_compared: Rule-based timeout triggers, heuristic retry counters, passive zero-shot LLM classifiers.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Requires fine-tuning SLM weights on domain-specific interaction traces; can suffer false alarms under benign exploratory human behavior.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Proactive intervention 3 steps prior to failure reduces task recovery time by 58% and prevents irrecoverable database corruption compared to reactive error catching.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Directly informs CausaGuard WP6 escalation engine: provides architecture for using compact, low-latency models to predict agent failure and trigger causal interventions proactively.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Beyond Ads: Sequential Decision-Making Algorithms in Law and Public Policy

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Peer-Reviewed Conference / Archival Survey & Analysis (arXiv:2112.06833v3, published in FAccT 2022). Comprehensive foundational analysis of sequential decision algorithms in high-stakes public domains.
field_04_concrete_problem: Failure of private-sector bandit and reinforcement learning assumptions (stationarity, unconfoundedness, unconstrained exploration) when applied to high-stakes legal, medical, and public policy domains (Section 1–3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: Long-horizon sequential decision agents operating under legal constraints, unobserved confounders, and statutory fairness requirements.
field_06_action_space: Discrete policy choices involving high-stakes resource allocation (e.g. judicial bail decisions, environmental inspections, regulatory enforcement audits).
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Evaluates statutory compliance, algorithmic disparate impact, and causal unobserved confounding sensitivity.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Formal taxonomy of domain failure modes in sequential decision systems: unobserved confounding in feedback loops, delayed and censored outcome labels, non-stationary policy environments, and constitutional non-discrimination constraints.
field_09_formal_assumptions: Standard unconfoundedness (A independent of Y(a) given X) is routinely violated in practical public policy deployments due to latent variables and selective enforcement.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Legal and ethical constraint boundary: mandates hard verification gates preventing algorithmic actions that breach procedural due process or statutory fairness quotas.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Analyzes sequential decision case studies across EPA environmental inspections, judicial pretrial risk assessments, and public health inspections (Section 4 & Table 1). Documents severe algorithmic failure when bandit feedback loops amplify systemic historical bias.
field_12_baselines_compared: Unconstrained Multi-Armed Bandits, Upper Confidence Bounds, Contextual Thompson Sampling, Static Heuristic Rules.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Standard bandit exploration strategies (e.g. epsilon-greedy) are legally and ethically unacceptable in safety-critical domains where assigning a suboptimal arm causes irreversible human harm.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Demonstrates that incorporating causal sensitivity analysis and safe baseline fallback mechanisms is essential to prevent self-reinforcing bias loops in autonomous decision systems.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct foundational motivation for CausaGuard high-stakes domain testing (WP6/WP7) and the overarching PhD thesis: proves why causal guardrails and safe baseline fallback are mandatory in real-world deployments.

field_02_bibliographic_record.title: Generalized Thompson Sampling for Sequential Decision-Making and Causal Inference

field_03_publication_tier: Tier-1 Foundational Archival Paper (arXiv:1303.4431v1). Seminal formulation uniting Thompson sampling with Pearl's causal inference and Bayesian decision theory.
field_04_concrete_problem: Resolving the fundamental distinction between observational data and experimental interventions in adaptive sequential control, unifying Thompson sampling with causal do-calculus (Section 1–3).
field_05_agent_architecture_horizon: General sequential decision agent interacting with an unknown reactive environment over infinite or indefinite discrete horizons.
field_06_action_space: Arbitrary discrete or structured action spaces A; formal distinction between observing action a (event A=a) and intervening to set action a (do(A=a)).
field_07_verifier_noise_delay: Bayesian posterior belief updater over causal environment models theta in Theta.
field_08_primary_method_algorithm: Generalized Thompson Sampling (GTS): samples an environment model theta from posterior belief P(theta | history), determines the causal optimal policy under theta, and executes action a according to interventional distribution P(a | do(theta)).
field_09_formal_assumptions: Environment belongs to a parameterized family of causal mechanisms; prior belief P(theta) has non-zero mass on the true causal environment.
field_10_authorization_security_layer: Causal intervention boundary: explicitly conditions on interventional distributions do(a) to avoid confounding observational correlations with true causal effects.
field_11_reported_evidence_benchmarks: Proves that standard Bayesian conditioning without causal distinction fails in non-Markovian or confounded environments (e.g. Newcomb's paradox, reactive POMDPs); proves GTS converges to the causally optimal intervention policy asymptotically (Section 4).
field_12_baselines_compared: Standard Bayesian Reinforcement Learning, naive Thompson Sampling, Q-learning.
field_13_limitations_failure_modes: Exact posterior calculation over causal environment spaces Theta is intractable for non-trivial continuous or open-world state spaces; relies on sampling or variational approximations.
field_14_disruption_recovery_findings: Shows that agents failing to distinguish between seeing and doing develop superstitious policies and fatal action loops; causal posterior sampling breaks superstitious feedback loops.
field_15_causaguard_relevance: Direct mathematical foundation for CausaGuard WP2 and WP3: provides the formal justification for why causal intervention modeling (P(Y | do(X))) is fundamentally required rather than correlational reward prediction.
